races.title: State House, District 28
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Larry C. Strickland
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 28 (southern Johnston County) since 2017. Served on the Johnston County Board of Education for about 18 years. Retired in 2016 from the NC Department of Transportation Right of Way Unit. Owns an appraisal business and co-owns a family farm.

endorsements.text: His campaign website says the NRA endorsed him in 2014. This is a campaign claim and I did not verify it elsewhere. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for him in the 2026 or 2024 elections.

cands.gaps: I found no documented actions or bills sponsored by Strickland on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site lists agriculture, transportation, health care, economic development, Second Amendment and education as issues, but it does not address data centers or most of those topics. I found no stated position from him on data centers or on development limits. The campaign site issues text appears old (it refers to Obamacare and a 2014 endorsement). His exact start year on the school board differs by source (1998 or 1999). His birthplace comes only from his own campaign website.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in Johnston County and has lived in Pine Level for 40 years; Wikipedia gives his birth date but not his birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2017, including as an Appropriations chair, and was on the Johnston County school board for about 18 years. Spent a career at NCDOT, retiring as Assistant Manager of the Right of Way Unit. Owns Strickland Appraisal Services, LLC and co-owns Strickland Brothers Farm, LLC.
qual.why: Nearly a decade of prior legislative service, a long stint in local elected office and business ownership put him in the high range. The committee chair post was not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Nearly a decade of prior legislative service, a long stint in local elected office and business ownership put him in the high range. The committee chair post was not counted toward the score.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign website says he will always fight for Second Amendment gun rights and notes an NRA endorsement in 2014.

cands.name: D. Matthew Bailey
cands.bio: D. Matthew Bailey was the Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 28 in 2026. He advanced without a primary contest and lost the general election to incumbent Republican Larry Strickland. The pages I had show no other offices held or jobs.

endorsements.text: Listed as recommended in two Sway voter guides: 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' (Tevin (Momala) Davis) and 'Waves of Democracy' (Terri Robinson).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Bailey was born or raised, when he moved to North Carolina, or his occupation and work history. We found no record of any elected office he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign site, interviews, or questionnaires, so we have no stated positions on data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or campaign money. We also found no controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements beyond two voter-guide groups.
